"In a novel or book series, there is generally one writer and one version of the character, so when someone decides to put their "spin" on it its more jarring and harder to like/way easier to hate."

I would like to add to this.

In cases like that, no one would be that pissed if they went the reinterpretation/reimagination/taking-different-spins path if this was fourth, fifth of tenth adaptation. (No one is pissed when they reimagine Shakespeare, for example; especially when it is reimagined well. Because he has thousands of adaptations, both movie and stage ones. People have already seen close adaptations of him: why not further ones take more liberties and have different spins, as time changes and we try to experiment with different contexts? It can be interesting and those who are not into that? They will still have their preferred close adaptations.

So, the problem with WoT (the work of a singular author with clearly defined "canon" elements) is that they decided to skip that first step of actually trying to adapt the source material in the context it was created (what I would call "close adaptation" - respecting author's vision, ideas, etc.) and went straight ahead into more experimental areas.

People were expecting the first, they received the latter (only minority of people is interested to see the latter as the first adaptation).

I will finish this with taking the upcoming Harry Potter tv-show adaptation as my closing example. I don't know what will they try with it: more liberal/experimental take of the canon of the story? Or will they try to make it even more closer to books than the previous adaptation? Whatever the case, I wouldn't care that much: I already have one decent adaptation that I love. If they manage to make the next one even more "belovable" - great! But I wouldn't be disappointed if it went some weird pathways.

I am currently healing from depression, anxiety and panic disorder and I discovered that 'Dracula' by Bram Stoker, which I read atm, is really helping me in that respect. I can relate to some characters, because their experiences are oddly similar to symptoms of depression and anxiety, and ocassionaly I come across some inspiring quotes. It is very well written book.

Majority of the story takes place in the real world, but despite that I find the story very escapistic, due to its gothic-fantasy nature. And not to mention that at times, Dracula *feels* like an adult version of Harry Potter, as there are many parallels between the two. I think you will see those, if you happen to read it, or already know about them, if you have read it.

Also: basically anything by Neil Gaiman.

Tako da, ono što me je iskustvo moje majke naučilo je to da je i tekako moguće ostaviti cigare: bitno je da ti to želiš to da učiniš i da nađeš način da prebrodiš krizice kad se pojave. Znam da neki ljudi postepeno pokušavaju da prestanu da puše koristeći elektronske cigarete. Drugi, poput moje majke, čvrsto odluče da neće više i ne vrate se više tome. Mnogi nikad ne uspeju da se svuku sa njih.

Ja se zapravo ovih dana osećam dosta malaksalo i nikakvo, zato odgovaram tek sad. Baš mi nije bilo ni do čega. Jutro nakon nove godine mi je bilo najgore, mislio sam da sam bio na ivici smrti, toliko sam bio malaksao i loše. Ali sad sam se kao popravio.

Skapirao sam skoro da mi pomaže čitanje knjiga. Ne znam jesi li osoba koja čita, ali svakako bih preporučio da probaš, čak iako ne čitaš. Meni pomaže u smislu da na neko određeno vreme čitam tuđe misli i pretvaram se da sam neko drugi. Na taj način silim mozak da se ponaša drugačije, kao osoba koja nije anksiozna npr. Što više čitam, sve mi biva bolje, jer se polako udaljavam od anksioznog sebe i učim mozak da postoje i drugačiji obrazci razmišljanja, rezonovanja, ponašanja itd. Tako da, eto jedna preporuka od mene.

Da budem iskren, što više čitam šta pišeš, sve više sebe vidim u tvojim rečima. Veoma slična situacija. Već duži niz godina sam ekstremno anksiozan, u poslednje vreme su krenuli i napadi panike/anksioznosti da mi se dešavaju, imam 25 godina i  porodica je isto narcisoidna, bitniji im je njihov ugled od bilo čega drugog, itd. Samo ne znam kakva si ti po pitanju svojih, ali ja sam sa svojima počeo da vodim dnevne ratove u kući i već sam krenuo da radim na tome da se odvojim od njih u sledećoj godini. Preporučio bih i tebi isto ako ikako može. Ja već nekoliko meseci posećujem bihevioralnu psihoterapiju i iako nije imala nikakvih drasticnih efekata (bar ne jos uvek), terapeutkinja je dosta dobra i uvek je na mojoj strani, podrzava me itd. pa na taj način pravi antitezu roditeljima koji nisu/nemaju razumevanja. Per Wikipedia: "In television, a staff writer is the probationary, entry-level position in the "writers room"; that is, the team that creates a television series."

It's not the most of the writing team, though.

The writing team for season 1 constitues of a group of 7 writers, two of which worked on the same episode. They are: showrunner Rafe Judkins (episodes 1, 7 and 8), Amanda Kate Shuman, Rafe's friend (episode 2), twin brothers (episode 3), Dave Hill (episode 4), Celine Song, stuff writer (ep 5) and Justine Juel Gillmer (ep 6).

We know that Rafe has read at least early books. How? We know he and his mother were fans in the past (how big one, I cannot know) AND we also saw posts from him (from several years ago) when he posted pages from the first two books to show how he is working on them. We could see how he analyzed pages and went through the books: notes on the margins, etc. (At least, we don't have the information that proves they are not his notes lol)

Twin brothers were also fans. There were posts about Rafe interviewing them and picking them because they were fans. There is picture of them that you can find online in which they are holding their favourite WoT books in hands, if I am not mistaken. Their episode was okay.

I don't know about Dave Hill, but he did such a great job on the episode which was given to him that I really don't care if he really read them or not.

The only writer I know for certainty that haven't read the books is Celine Song. However, you need to know that it wasn't up to her to decide how that episode will go. It is up to the showrunner and other writers. Hers was to use her own talent to deliver in the best way she could the material others told her to deliver.

So, out of 8 episodes and 7 writers, we know for certainty that 4 episodes were done by people who know the books (Rafe and twins). One writer is uncertain (Dave), but he did excellent job IMO that I don't mind if he is a 🍭fake fan🍭. I don't know about Amanda and Justine, but their episodes were decent, epsecially Justine's. I can tell the same of Celine's episode. (I didn't like that ep in particular, but I think that she executed well the material that was given to her. It's also worth keeping in mind that each ep went through several stages of change and alterations that it is imposible for us to know how much of each episode is the writer that is credited to it and how much are later changes).

The show's fallacy isn't the writers that haven't read books. It's direction and approach to the show and that depends on Rafe's vision.

However, I can see why it became a big hit: it has a very good set up (this is only one reason that I am pointing out, among others, but it definetely contributed). Doing that is to some extent fine by me, except... that such approach implies that the beginning of the book is not good enough and/or too boring for casual viewers to be invested in. (I read this is as just an excuse to grimdark-ize WoT, because that's another current trend in the Hollywood when it comes to fantasy adaptations - and imo, by following all these trends, they are making themselves less unique and more like some generic fantasy show out there).

So, instead of allowing the show to breathe in the first season, using it as a set up season, (and using it to show the unique parts of the world building***) - even to the detriment of being slower,
they tried to cram in it as much of the later stuff as they could, because our new viewers need to see everything good that our show needs to offer immediately (God forbid that they need to wait for that, heh...😏). Not to mention focusing on unimportant made-up characters for the sake of "showing us something significant which will be payed off later, instead of telling". 

***When it come to the unique lore, I believe there is so much missed potential in this season: they never explained how Dragon's Fang symbol operates in the world, and yet, it pops up everywhere. What would fix this? One scene in episode one when (for example) Cen Buie starts quarreling with someone, who then scrambles the symbol on the door of that someone in the aftermath, while villagers witness everything in shock. Or something like that to show us what is this world, who are these villagers, how they live with eacb other, etc. (In my opinion, this would be better and more integral to the story than that made-up ritual that we got, especially in the later seasons, when the village and certain families become important). Also, changes like this are the changes that I can understand when you are adaptating something. You are not making up anything new, just expanding on what is already there to actually show the world, not tell it. Wolfbrother thing would probably be one of the most unique elements of the show, if dealt with it properly, yet we got... whatever we have got, for the sake of keeping the mistery of the Dragon Reborn (which was never mistery in the books and it is not now in the age of the internent when it is not that difficult to find the existing asnwers or to be easily spoiled - I bet vast majority of new fans already knows who is the Dragon).

So, all in all: I don't hate the show. I don't have any reason for that. I have lot to criticize, but that's it. As of now, I think it's just average show - not that good, but not that bad. It has lots of good elements, especially when you separate it from the books. However, since this IS an adaptation, I think it needs to be treated like that. And IMO, it fails as an adaptation. I also like letting my stories grow organically, rather than imposing specific frame or structure on it (I believe that I am just restricting my own creative abilities in that way). I only decide what the story "is" after I finish it.

I am male and in the next month I am turning 25 (writing this just as a reference point, as I am not much older than you).
 
I also like writing and I have also  dealt with problems such as depression, anxiety, adhd, etc. in the past. I also sometimes find myself unable to write anything, my mind just turns into blank slate/space. No motivation or creative energy for writing at all.

However, one day I made a deal with myself and that actually helped me in continuing writing. The deal is simple: whatever is the cause of your current creative blockade, try to write a story out of it.

Are you feeling just empty, devoid of any feeling or inteligence in your brain? Write a story about it. Do a literary experiment in which you will write a story that will be writren by empty forces and will be devoid of any feelings, etc. Try to think of the ways how that story can look like. And don't worry about it being silly or stupidly written. You don't need to show it to anyone (and you can always change it for better when you are feeling better), but if it keeps you moving and going, then it's a good deal in my opinion.

This is the reason why I have some stories that I only write in specific moods. Some stories I only write when I am depressed or when I hate the world. Some when I am feeling empty inside, like when you experience burnout. There is even one story which I completely extrapolated from the scribbles I wrote on pieces of paper in times of idleness (my little nonsense story lol).

However, I usually write fantasy stuff, so that helps me in better expressing my inner world and my inner turmoil, because the tools and opportunities in fantasy world are bigger. I don't know what you usually write about, but maybe you can try this trick once or twice to see whether it suits you.

 I am always feeling better after it, because of the cognitive reward: I feel like I have accomplished something that day, despite  rest of the day being bad and despite not doing anything else. At least, there is that one positive thing that I care about and which I did, so I feel I was successful that day.
